en.usage: Ordinal numbers, ranking, numbers (house numbers, buses, trains)
en.notes: 一番 (ichiban) also means "the most" and is used as a superlative: 一番高い = the most expensive. No sound changes.
examples[].german: What is your favorite food?
Please take bus number 3.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとばん and ふたばん. 一晩中 (ひとばんじゅう) = "all night long".
examples[].german: I studied all night.
I stayed two nights at my friend's house.

en.usage: Position in a sequence: the second seat, the third door
en.notes: 番目 turns a number into an ordinal: 一番目 = the first. Unlike 一番 (number one; "the most"), 番目 emphasizes position in a series. No sound changes. Similar: 目 after a counter (二つ目, 三人目) and the prefix 第.
examples[].german: Please sit in the third seat from the front.
He is the second tallest among the siblings.

en.usage: Platform or track number in a station
en.notes: Typical station announcement: 〜番線に電車が参ります. 番 = number, 線 = line/track. No sound changes.
examples[].german: The train to Tokyo leaves from track 2.
A train will shortly arrive on track 3.

en.notes: Since びん already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes.
examples[].german: I ordered two bottles of wine.
Please buy a bottle of milk.

en.notes: Since びん already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes. Often used for flight numbers and postal services.
examples[].german: The next flight departs at 14:00.
There are three bus services a day.

en.notes: No sound changes. Note: 一部 (いちぶ) as a counter = "one copy", but 一部 can also mean "a part" (e.g. 一部の人 = some people).
examples[].german: Please make ten copies of this document.
One newspaper, please.

en.notes: Since ぶん already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes. Don't confuse with 分 (ぶん, share/portion).
examples[].german: Please write three sentences in Japanese.
The first sentence is very important.

en.notes: No sound changes. The base reading びょう stays unchanged. Time units: 分 (ふん) = minutes, 秒 (びょう) = seconds. 三分二十秒 = 3 minutes 20 seconds.
examples[].german: I ran a hundred meters in ten seconds.
It starts in three seconds.

en.notes: Mainly used for outerwear. For flat garments such as T-shirts, 枚 is often used too. 着 also means "arrival" (到着).
examples[].german: I bought a dress.
I have three suits.

en.notes: Mainly used for tofu. 一丁 can also colloquially mean "Let's go!".
examples[].german: I bought a block of tofu.
Two servings of cold tofu, please.

en.notes: Part of the Japanese address system: 区 (く) → 町 (まち/ちょう) → 丁目 → 番地. "三丁目の夕日" (Always: Sunset on Third Street) is a famous Japanese film.
examples[].german: The address is Kabukichō 1-chōme, Shinjuku ward.
There is a convenience store on the corner of the third block.

en.notes: No sound changes - a simple counter. Used for all mechanical or electronic devices.
examples[].german: There are two cars.
I bought a computer.

en.usage: Prefix before the number in formal enumerations: 第一回, 第二章, 第三位
en.notes: 第 goes before the number, often together with a counter: 第一回 (the first time, the first installment), 第二章 (chapter 2), 第三位 (third place). More formal than 番目. No sound changes; besides だいよん, だいなな and だいきゅう, だいし, だいしち and だいく also occur. 第九（だいく）is Beethoven's Ninth, traditionally performed in Japan at the end of the year.
examples[].german: The first meeting is next Monday.
At the end of the year, Beethoven's Ninth is performed everywhere.
specialCounts[].note: less common than だいよん

en.usage: Stair steps, shelves, martial-arts ranks (judo, karate), go ranks
en.notes: No sound changes. Used for ranks in martial arts (初段 = first dan). In grammar: 一段動詞 (いちだんどうし) = ichidan verb, 五段動詞 (ごだんどうし) = godan verb.
examples[].german: He is a third-dan in judo.
This staircase has fifty steps.

en.usage: Temperature, angles, frequency (more formal than 回)
en.notes: No sound changes. 一度 (いちど) = "once" is very common. 何度も (なんども) = "again and again". As temperature: 38度 (さんじゅうはちど) = 38 degrees (e.g. a fever).
examples[].german: It's 30 degrees today.
I'd like to go to Japan once.

en.notes: No sound changes. The exchange rate is 為替レート（かわせレート）; for yen, see the counter 円.
examples[].german: This shirt cost twenty dollars.
How many yen is one dollar worth right now?

en.usage: Train stations, stops along a route
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとえき and ふたえき. Very useful when navigating the Japanese rail system.
examples[].german: It's three stations from here.
Let's walk one station.

en.notes: 4円 = よえん (not よんえん). 五円 (ごえん) sounds like ご縁 (fate/connection), so 5-yen coins are offered at shrines as good-luck charms.
examples[].german: That costs 500 yen.
With a thousand-yen bill, please.

en.usage: Doses of medicine, servings of medication
en.notes: 一服 (いっぷく) also colloquially means "to take a (smoking) break". Used for powdered or herbal medicines.
examples[].german: I took one dose of herbal medicine.
Let's take a break.

en.usage: Plastic bags, paper bags, bags of food
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとふくろ and ふたふくろ. As a multi-syllable kun counter, it has no typical sound changes at 3, 6, 8, 10.
examples[].german: I bought two bags of sweets.
A plastic bag at the register costs three yen.

en.usage: Minutes in clock times and durations
en.notes: Especially many sound changes! ふん changes to ぷん at 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10. 十分 (じゅっぷん) as minutes vs. 十分 (じゅうぶん) = "enough".
examples[].german: Please wait five minutes.
It takes ten minutes to the station.
specialCounts[].note: はん (半) = half, e.g. 三時半 = half past three

en.notes: 4月 = しがつ (not よんがつ), 7月 = しちがつ (not なながつ), 9月 = くがつ (not きゅうがつ). Don't confuse with ヶ月 (かげつ) = duration in months!
examples[].german: Cherry blossoms bloom in March or April.
In Japan, the new school year starts in April.

en.usage: Rice (1合 ≈ 180 ml), sake, traditional Japanese unit of volume
en.notes: 1合 ≈ 180 ml. When climbing Mt. Fuji, 合 marks the stations from 一合目 to 十合目 (summit). 一升 (いっしょう) = 10合.
examples[].german: I cooked three gō of rice.
I went up to the fifth station of Mt. Fuji.
specialCounts[].note: Fifth station (e.g. on the Mt. Fuji climb)

en.notes: Since ご already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes. Don't confuse with the meaning "language" (日本語, 英語, etc.).
examples[].german: I learn ten new words every day.
This sentence consists of five words.

en.usage: Car number on trains, especially the Shinkansen and for reserved seats
en.notes: 号 = number, 車 = car. Markings on the platform show where each car stops. No sound changes.
examples[].german: The reserved seats are in car 7.
It is seat 12A in car 3.

en.usage: Weight; when shopping, often given per 100 g (百グラム)
en.notes: No sound changes. Kilogram: キログラム or short キロ.
examples[].german: Three hundred grams of pork, please.
This meat costs 200 yen per 100 grams.

en.usage: Lines of text, lines of code
en.notes: Since ぎょう already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes. 行 also has the reading こう (e.g. 銀行) and いく/ゆく (to go).
examples[].german: This poem is written in five lines.
Please summarize the report in three lines.

en.usage: Cups, glasses, bowls (coffee, tea, rice, beer)
en.notes: Same sound-change pattern as 本: は→ば (after ん) and ぱ (after っ). いっぱい also means "full" or "a lot"!
examples[].german: I drank a cup of coffee.
I ordered three glasses of beer.

en.usage: Losses in sports competitions, games, tournaments
en.notes: Follows the h sound-change pattern like 杯. Almost always used together with 勝 (しょう), e.g. 十勝二敗 (じゅっしょうにはい). Note: 一敗 (いっぱい) sounds like いっぱい (full/a lot)!
examples[].german: We've only lost once this season.
The record is five wins and three losses.

en.notes: No sound changes. Very common in everyday use: 二倍 = twice, 三倍 = three times. 人一倍 (ひといちばい) = "more than others".
examples[].german: Rent in Tokyo is three times as high as in the countryside.
I ordered double the amount.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとはこ and ふたはこ. As a multi-syllable kun counter, it has no typical sound changes.
examples[].german: I ordered a box of mandarin oranges.
I received three boxes of chocolate.

en.usage: Hotel nights, trip length in nights
en.notes: 二泊三日 (にはくみっか) = "2 nights, 3 days" is the typical Japanese way to describe a trip. Same sound-change patterns as 杯: は→ぱ at 1, 3, 6, 8, 10.
examples[].german: I'm going on a trip of two nights and three days.
How much is one night?

en.notes: Follows the h sound-change pattern: 1→いっぱつ, 3→さんぱつ, 6→ろっぱつ, 8→はっぱつ, 10→じゅっぱつ. 一発 (いっぱつ) is also used idiomatically for "on the first try".
examples[].german: Five fireworks were launched.
I hit it on the first shot.

en.usage: Stories, parts of a work (前編 = first part, 後編 = second part)
en.notes: 前編 (ぜんぺん) = first part, 後編 (こうへん) = second part, 短編 (たんぺん) = short story, 長編 (ちょうへん) = novel/full-length work.
examples[].german: I read three short stories.
This film is split into two parts.

en.usage: Rooms in hotels, apartments (more informal than 室)
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとへや and ふたへや; for 3, besides さんへや you can also hear the traditional みへや. へや does not become voiced (べや). More informal than 室. In sumo, 部屋 means a training stable.
examples[].german: This apartment has three rooms.
Is there a room available?

en.usage: Cats, dogs, fish, insects, small to medium-sized animals
en.notes: Same sound-change patterns as 本 and 杯: ひ→び (after ん) and ぴ (after っ). For large animals, 頭 is used.
examples[].german: I have two cats.
Five fish are swimming.

en.notes: Follows the h sound-change pattern. 散歩 (さんぽ) = "walk, stroll" contains the same 歩 and the same sound change! 一歩 (いっぽ) = "one step" is also used figuratively for "a step forward".
examples[].german: I walk ten thousand steps every day.
"Sanpo" (a stroll) comes from "three steps".

en.usage: Pens, bottles, umbrellas, trees, films, phone calls
en.notes: A classic example of sound changes: ほん → ぼん (after ん) and ぽん (after っ). Also used for abstractly "long" things such as films and calls.
examples[].german: I have three pens.
I watched one movie.

en.notes: Watch out: 4時 = よじ (not よんじ), 7時 = しちじ (not ななじ), 9時 = くじ (not きゅうじ). These exceptions are often tested!
examples[].german: It is three o'clock now.
I get up at seven.

en.notes: For 4, よじ (not よんじ) is used. 四字熟語 (よじじゅくご) is a well-known term for four-character kanji idioms. Since じ begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes.
examples[].german: The name is four kanji long.
The password must be at least eight characters.

en.notes: No sound changes. Used mainly at schools and universities. 目 (め) is added as an ordinal suffix.
examples[].german: I have classes until sixth period today.
Third period is math.

en.notes: No sound changes. Common at pharmacies and doctors: 一日三回、一回二錠 = "three times a day, two tablets each time".
examples[].german: Take two tablets of this medicine each time.
Could I have a headache tablet?

en.usage: Room size in tatami units (1畳 ≈ 1.65 m²)
en.notes: For 4, よじょう (not よんじょう) is used. 四畳半 (よじょうはん) is the classic room size for tea ceremonies. Since じょう begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes.
examples[].german: My room is six tatami mats big.
There is a Japanese-style room of four and a half tatami.
specialCounts[].note: Classic room size for tea ceremonies

en.usage: Lessons in textbooks, chapters in language courses
en.notes: Follows the k sound-change pattern: 1→いっか, 6→ろっか, 8→はっか, 10→じゅっか. Typical of Japanese textbooks such as "みんなの日本語" or "Genki".
examples[].german: Today we'll study lesson three.
This textbook goes up to lesson twenty.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとかぶ and ふたかぶ. In finance, 株 also means "stock/share": 株価 (かぶか) = share price, 株式 (かぶしき) = shares.
examples[].german: I planted three tomato seedlings.
I own a hundred shares of this company.

en.notes: ヶ is also written as か, カ or 箇. Don't confuse with the month names (一月 = いちがつ = January)!
examples[].german: I studied Japanese for six months.
A baby is born after ten months.

en.usage: Shopping baskets, laundry baskets, fruit baskets
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとかご and ふたかご. Used for baskets with contents.
examples[].german: I bought two baskets of strawberries.
A basket of laundry has piled up.

en.notes: 3階 is さんがい (not さんかい) - a frequently tested exception! The question word 何階 is read なんがい.
examples[].german: My room is on the third floor.
I took the elevator up to the fifth floor.

en.notes: Unlike 階, 回 has no sound change at 3: さんかい (not さんがい).
examples[].german: I have been to Japan three times.
Please try it once.

en.notes: Follows the k sound-change pattern: 1→いっかこく, 6→ろっかこく, 8→はっかこく, 10→じゅっかこく. ヶ国語 (かこくご) is used for the number of languages.
examples[].german: I can speak three languages.
I visited five countries in Europe.

en.notes: Used for all kinds of cans, both beverage cans and canned food.
examples[].german: I bought three cans of beer.
It's juice at a hundred yen per can.

en.notes: Used specifically for nigiri sushi. In sushi restaurants, orders often come in pairs (二貫 = one pair).
examples[].german: Two pieces of tuna sushi, please.
Today I ate a whole ten pieces of sushi.

en.usage: Manga volumes, book series, film series
en.notes: Very common for manga and book series. Same reading and sound changes as the counter 缶 (かん, cans).
examples[].german: I bought volume one hundred of One Piece.
This series has twenty volumes in total.

en.usage: Places, locations, spots (e.g. mistakes in a text, tourist attractions)
en.notes: A very common counter for places and spots. Can also be written 箇所.
examples[].german: There are three mistakes.
I visited five temples in Kyoto.

en.notes: 三軒 = さんげん (not さんけん) - the sound changes to the voiced が-row after ん. 一軒家 (いっけんや) = detached house is a common compound.
examples[].german: There are five restaurants on this street.
I live in a detached house.
specialCounts[].note: Known from 三軒茶屋 (Sangenjaya) in Tokyo

en.notes: Common in business and formal contexts. 事件 (じけん) = incident/event. Same sound-change patterns as 軒.
examples[].german: There were ten inquiries today.
Let's talk about that matter.

en.notes: Japan has 47 administrative units: 1都 (Tokyo), 1道 (Hokkaido), 2府 (Osaka, Kyoto), 43県. Together: 都道府県 (とどうふけん).
examples[].german: There are seven prefectures in the Kantō region.
I traveled through all 47 prefectures of Japan.

en.notes: Used for airplanes and helicopters. Sound changes at 1, 6, 8, 10.
examples[].german: Five airplanes are parked at the airport.
Two helicopters are flying.

en.usage: Business quarters, anime seasons, terms of office
en.notes: Often used for anime seasons and business periods. 一期一会 (いちごいちえ) = "one time, one meeting" (a famous Japanese concept).
examples[].german: The second season of this anime has started.
The company president has entered his third term.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた; from 3 on the regular on readings are used.
examples[].german: I ate two slices of bread.
I ordered three slices of sashimi.

en.usage: Short form of キログラム (weight) and キロメートル (distance); also km/h: 時速六十キロ
en.notes: キロ alone can mean kilogram or kilometer - context decides. Often written kg or km. Sound change at 6 (ろっキロ) and 10 (じゅっキロ), optionally also at 8 (はっキロ).
examples[].german: It is about two kilometers to the station.
This watermelon weighs a whole five kilos.

en.usage: Small, compact items (apples, eggs, balls, etc.)
en.notes: Universal counter for small, compact objects. Can also be used as a general counter when you don't know the specific one.
examples[].german: Three apples, please.
I bought six eggs.

en.usage: Homes, houses (in statistics and real estate)
en.notes: 一戸建て (いっこだて) = detached house is a very common expression. Used in news and statistics for dwelling units.
examples[].german: Fifty households lost power because of the typhoon.
I want to live in a detached house.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとこま and ふたこま. 四コマ漫画 (よんこままんが) = four-panel manga is a popular format in Japan. At universities, timetable slots are counted as コマ.
examples[].german: I have three class periods today.
I like four-panel comics.

en.notes: 4時間 = よじかん (not よんじかん), 9時間 = くじかん (not きゅうじかん). Same exceptions as for clock time (時).
examples[].german: I sleep eight hours every day.
It takes two and a half hours from Tokyo to Osaka.

en.notes: 俳句 (はいく) = haiku contains the kanji 句. Used for short Japanese poems and set phrases.
examples[].german: I memorized three haiku by Matsuo Bashō.
Try composing a verse.

en.usage: Bites of food; also bank accounts, donations, subscription shares
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた. A versatile counter: besides mouthfuls, it is also used for bank accounts and donations.
examples[].german: Please try a bite.
I signed up for two donation shares.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとくみ and ふたくみ. From 3 on, the on reading is used. In schools, 組 refers to the class (e.g. 一組 = Class 1).
examples[].german: Two pairs of chopsticks, please.
I'm in Class 2 of the third year.

en.usage: Chairs, tables and stools (rather formal or written)
en.notes: In everyday speech, chairs are often simply counted with つ or 個; 脚 is more formal (inventory lists, furniture trade). Sound change as with counters starting with k.
examples[].german: Please bring ten chairs to the meeting room.
This table comes with four chairs.

en.notes: Also used for classical music and instrumental pieces. 名曲 (めいきょく) = masterpiece (music).
examples[].german: I sang five songs at karaoke.
The new album contains twelve songs.

en.notes: Used mainly for board games such as shōgi and go. 局 also means "office/bureau" (郵便局 = post office).
examples[].german: I played three games of shōgi.
It's the fifth game of a best-of-seven match.

en.usage: Traditional Japanese rooms, room counts in real estate
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた. Used for traditional Japanese rooms and in real estate listings.
examples[].german: This house has three rooms.
I turned one room into a study.

en.usage: Paper, plates, T-shirts, tickets, slices, sheets
en.notes: One of the easiest counters - no sound changes! Used for anything flat and thin.
examples[].german: I bought five stamps.
How many sheets of paper are there?

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとまく and ふたまく. 幕間 (まくあい) = intermission between acts.
examples[].german: This play has three acts.
The first act has begun.

en.usage: Lengths and distances; often written m
en.notes: Loanword from French (mètre). No sound changes. Centimeter: センチ, kilometer: キロ(メートル).
examples[].german: This pool is 25 meters long.
There is a police box a hundred meters ahead.

en.usage: Formal counting of people (reservations, forms, announcements)
en.notes: Formal version of 人. Used in restaurants (三名様), for reservations and in official contexts. No sound changes.
examples[].german: The party of three waiting.
There are twenty participants.

en.usage: Restaurants and service: number of guests
en.notes: Polite form of 名（めい）, used by staff to count guests. About yourself you don't say 名様, but e.g. 三人です or 三名です. For one or two guests you usually hear お一人様／お二人様.
examples[].german: Welcome! How many people?
Mr./Ms. Tanaka, party of four, please.

en.usage: Mirrors, tennis courts, newspaper pages, wall surfaces
en.notes: No sound changes. 一面 (いちめん) also means "one side" or the front page of a newspaper.
examples[].german: There are three tennis courts.
It was on the front page of the newspaper.

en.usage: Test questions, exam problems, quiz questions
en.notes: No sound changes. Used for questions on tests and exams. 何問 (なんもん) = "How many questions?"
examples[].german: The test has ten questions in total.
I got three out of five questions right.

en.usage: Duration in years, calendar years, school years
en.notes: 4年 = よねん (not よんねん). Duration: ～年間 (ねんかん). 今年 (ことし) = this year, 来年 (らいねん) = next year, 去年 (きょねん) = last year.
examples[].german: I lived in Japan for three years.
This year is 2026.

en.usage: Days of the month (dates) and duration in days
en.notes: 1日-10日 and 20日 use the traditional Japanese readings (kun-yomi) and are completely irregular. From 11日 on, ～にち is used (じゅういちにち, じゅうににち, etc.). 一日 has two meanings: ついたち (the 1st of the month) and いちにち (one whole day).
examples[].german: I was in Kyoto for three days.
My birthday is May 20.
specialCounts[].note: As a date: the 1st of the month. As a duration: いちにち (one day).

en.notes: 1 and 2 are completely irregular (ひとり, ふたり). From 3 on, にん is used.
examples[].german: There are three students.
I came alone.

en.usage: Servings for a given number of people (in cooking, at restaurants)
en.notes: No sound changes. 一人前 (いちにんまえ) also has the figurative meaning "full-fledged/grown-up": 一人前の大人 = a full-fledged adult. Very common in restaurants.
examples[].german: I ordered two servings of gyoza.
This recipe serves four.

en.notes: 300 = さんびゃく, 600 = ろっぴゃく, 800 = はっぴゃく (sound changes!)
3000 = さんぜん, 8000 = はっせん (sound changes!)
Japanese counts in units of 10,000 rather than in thousands.
し (shi) is the on reading, よん (yon) is the kun reading. よん is preferred because し can also mean "death" (死).
なな (nana) is often preferred because しち can be confused with いち (1).
きゅう (kyū) is more common. く (ku) can mean "suffering" (苦) and is avoided.
Sound change as with counters starting with p: いっ-, ろっ-, はっ-, じゅっパーセント. For 10% steps you can also say 割（わり）: 三割 = 30%.
examples[].german: The chance of rain tomorrow is 70 percent.
Everything is ten percent off.
specialCounts[].note: besides じゅっパーセント

en.usage: Cartons of milk, cartons of juice, ready-made packs
en.notes: Loanword from English "pack". As a katakana counter, it has no sound changes. Very common in the supermarket.
examples[].german: I bought two cartons of milk.
Natto is sold in packs of three.

en.notes: Loanword from English "page". As a katakana counter, it has no sound changes.
examples[].german: Please open your textbook to page thirty.
This book has two hundred pages.

en.usage: Queues, rows of seats, rows in a table
en.notes: No sound changes. 一列 (いちれつ) = "one row" is very common. 行列 (ぎょうれつ) = queue. 列目 (れつめ) is used for the ordinal: 三列目 = "third row".
examples[].german: Please line up in a single row.
The seats are in the third row.

en.notes: No sound changes. 一輪車 (いちりんしゃ) = unicycle, 二輪車 (にりんしゃ) = motorcycle/two-wheeler, 四輪車 (よんりんしゃ) = car. 五輪 (ごりん) = the five Olympic rings = the Olympic Games.
examples[].german: A single rose is blooming in the garden.
"Gorin" (five rings) is another name for the Olympics.

en.usage: Liquids and volume; written L or ℓ
en.notes: No sound changes. Milliliter: ミリリットル (ml).
examples[].german: I drink two liters of water every day.
This car runs twenty kilometers on one liter of gasoline.

en.usage: Names the bases in baseball (一塁 = first base) and counts bases covered on hits (二塁打 = double)
en.notes: No sound changes. Baseball is very popular in Japan. 一塁 = first base, 二塁 = second base, 三塁 = third base. 本塁 (ほんるい) = home plate. 盗塁 (とうるい) = stolen base.
examples[].german: The runner is on first base.
He hit a double.

en.notes: Used exclusively for railway cars and tram cars. No sound changes, since りょう begins with r.
examples[].german: This train consists of ten cars.
Please board the third car from the front.

en.notes: 20歳 = はたち is one of the best-known exceptions in Japanese. 才 is a simplified way of writing 歳.
examples[].german: I am 25 years old.
My daughter turned three.
specialCounts[].note: Completely irregular! An important age (coming of age).

en.usage: Spoons as a cooking measure (大さじ = tablespoon, 小さじ = teaspoon)
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとさじ and ふたさじ. 大さじ (おおさじ) = tablespoon (15 ml), 小さじ (こさじ) = teaspoon (5 ml). "さじを投げる" (saji o nageru) = "to throw the spoon" = to give up.
examples[].german: Add two tablespoons of soy sauce.
Add one teaspoon of sugar.

en.usage: Fishing rods, laundry poles, bamboo poles
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとさお and ふたさお. Also used for tansu chests (箪笥): 一竿 = one chest.
examples[].german: I own two fishing rods.
I bought a laundry pole.

en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた. Especially common at conveyor-belt sushi (回転寿司).
examples[].german: I ate five plates at the conveyor-belt sushi restaurant.
I ordered a plate of salad.

en.notes: Sound changes at 1 (いっさつ), 8 (はっさつ), 10 (じゅっさつ).
examples[].german: I read three books.
One magazine, please.

en.notes: No sound changes. Used both for family generations and for technology generations.
examples[].german: Three generations live together.
It is a fifth-generation smartphone.

en.notes: Used for seats in restaurants, theaters, airplanes and other public venues.
examples[].german: Are two seats available?
This restaurant has fifty seats in total.

en.notes: Used for larger ships and boats. For small boats, 艘 (そう) can also be used.
examples[].german: Three ships are moored in the harbor.
A fishing boat has left the port.

en.notes: Used for train and subway lines. Famous lines: 山手線 (やまのてせん), 中央線 (ちゅうおうせん), 東海道線 (とうかいどうせん).
examples[].german: Many lines run through Tokyo Station.
Please transfer to the Yamanote Line.

en.usage: Short form of センチメートル; body height, small lengths
en.notes: Short form of センチメートル (cm). Sound change as with counters starting with s: いっセンチ, はっセンチ, じゅっセンチ.
examples[].german: I am 165 centimeters tall.
Please make it three centimeters shorter.

en.notes: Follows the s sound-change pattern: 1→いっせたい, 8→はっせたい, 10→じゅっせたい. 二世帯住宅 (にせたいじゅうたく) = two-family house is a common term in Japan.
examples[].german: Fifty households live in this apartment building.
We live in a two-family house.

en.notes: Used for sections of texts, verses in songs and paragraphs in academic writing. In sports, also for matchdays in a league.
examples[].german: This song has three verses.
Please sing the second verse.

en.notes: No sound changes. 試合 is the general word for sports games in Japanese.
examples[].german: There are three games today.
The first game is in the morning.

en.notes: Formal counter for rooms. In everyday speech 部屋 (へや) is more common; 室 is typical of hotels and official statements.
examples[].german: This hotel has a hundred rooms in total.
Only one room is available.

en.notes: Often used with the prefix 第 (だい): 第一章, 第二章, etc.
examples[].german: I finished reading the third chapter.
This novel has twelve chapters in total.

en.notes: No sound changes. 第一位 (だいいちい) = first place. Used for rankings, sports results and statistics.
examples[].german: I came third in the marathon.
Japan's population ranks eleventh in the world.

en.usage: Wins in sports competitions, games, tournaments
en.notes: Follows the sh sound-change pattern: 1→いっしょう, 8→はっしょう, 10→じゅっしょう. Often used together with 敗 (はい): 三勝二敗 = 3 wins, 2 losses.
examples[].german: This season the record is ten wins and five losses.
The team won three times.

en.usage: Meals per day, meals included on trips
en.notes: 一日三食 (いちにちさんしょく) = "three meals a day" is a very common expression. For hotels: 一泊二食付き = one night with breakfast and dinner included.
examples[].german: I eat three meals a day.
It is a plan with one night and two meals.

en.usage: Laps on a track, circuits, trips around something
en.notes: Follows the sh sound-change pattern: 1→いっしゅう, 8→はっしゅう, 10→じゅっしゅう. 世界一周 (せかいいっしゅう) = "trip around the world" is a famous expression.
examples[].german: I ran three laps around the schoolyard.
I set off on a trip around the world.

en.notes: Follows the sh sound-change pattern: 1→いっしゅ, 8→はっしゅ, 10→じゅっしゅ. Mostly used as 種類 (しゅるい): 三種類 = "three kinds/types".
examples[].german: This restaurant has three kinds of curry.
I planted five kinds of flowers.

en.notes: Sound changes at 1 (いっしゅうかん), 8 (はっしゅうかん), 10 (じゅっしゅうかん). Don't confuse with 習慣 (しゅうかん = habit).
examples[].german: I was in Japan for two weeks.
I exercise three times a week.

en.usage: Footwear worn in pairs (shoes, socks, stockings, boots)
en.notes: Always counts pairs, not individual shoes/socks. Sound changes at 1 (いっそく), 3 (さんぞく), 8 (はっそく), 10 (じゅっそく).
examples[].german: I bought two pairs of shoes.
The socks come in a set of three pairs.

en.notes: Used more in literary writing or seafaring for small boats. In everyday speech, 隻 is often used for all types of ships.
examples[].german: Two boats are floating on the lake.
We crossed the river in a small boat.

en.notes: 一層 (いっそう) is also used as an adverb meaning "even more, all the more".
examples[].german: I baked a three-layer cake.
It is necessary to make even more effort.

en.usage: Bouquets, stacks of paper, bundles of banknotes, bundles of straw
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひとたば and ふたたば. 一束 (ひとたば) of flowers is a very common expression when buying flowers.
examples[].german: I bought a bunch of flowers.
Please bundle the documents into three stacks.

en.notes: 一体 (いったい) is also used as an adverb meaning "on earth, ever": 一体何が起きたの？= What on earth happened? Used for statues, corpses and robots/dolls.
examples[].german: There are three Buddha statues in this temple.
Two robots are on display.

en.usage: Round things (cabbage, onions, balls of yarn)
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた. Used for round, ball-shaped items, especially heads of cabbage and portions of udon.
examples[].german: I bought a head of cabbage.
Please boil two portions of udon.

en.usage: Eye drops, medicine drops, drops of liquid
en.notes: Follows the t sound-change pattern: 1→いってき, 8→はってき, 10→じゅってき. 一滴 (いってき) is also used poetically: 一滴も〜ない = "not a single drop".
examples[].german: Put two drops in each eye.
I drank the water down to the last drop.

en.notes: 点 is used in two contexts: points/scores (百点 = 100 points) and as a formal counter for items (especially in retail and museums).
examples[].german: I got 90 points on the test.
You are buying three items.

en.notes: 初戦 (しょせん) = first match, 決勝戦 (けっしょうせん) = final. Frequently used in sports news.
examples[].german: This season I played ten matches and won seven.
I won the first match.

en.notes: Used for whole buildings or building wings, not for individual rooms.
examples[].german: This housing complex has five apartment buildings.
Two new buildings were constructed.

en.usage: Number of methods, variants or solutions
en.notes: 1 and 2 are read the native way: ひととおり, ふたとおり. Not to be confused with 通（つう）for letters. 一通り also means "roughly, once through": 資料に一通り目を通す.
examples[].german: There are two ways to solve this problem.
There are six combinations in total.

en.usage: Horses, cows, elephants, whales - large animals
en.notes: Used for animals roughly human-sized or larger. Few sound changes (1, 8, 10).
examples[].german: There are three horses in the pasture.
There is an elephant at the zoo.

en.usage: General counter for things (1-10), used when you don't know the specific counter
en.notes: The most important counter! Uses the native Japanese (kun) readings of the numbers. Only available for 1-10; from 11 on you must use a specific counter. Also commonly used for the age of small children (三つ = 3 years old).
examples[].german: Three apples, please.
There are two reasons.

en.notes: Japan is an island nation. 本州 (ほんしゅう), 北海道 (ほっかいどう), 九州 (きゅうしゅう), 四国 (しこく) are the four main islands.
examples[].german: Japan consists of over six thousand islands.
I joined a tour around three islands.

en.notes: Used for ports (港) and also for airports (空港). 五港 (ごこう) is historically known as the five treaty ports of the Meiji era.
examples[].german: Japan has five important ports.
It is a cruise calling at three ports.

en.usage: Grains of rice, pearls, seeds, pills
en.notes: 1 and 2 use the kun readings ひと and ふた. Used for very small, grain-like or round objects.
examples[].german: Please take two pills.
Don't waste a single grain of rice.

en.notes: 一対 (いっつい) = one matching pair. Unlike 組 (set/group), 対 emphasizes symmetrical pairing.
examples[].german: A pair of vases is on display.
I bought a pair of earrings.

en.notes: Also used for modern communication such as emails. 一通り (ひととおり) = "once through, in general" is a related, common expression.
examples[].german: I sent three emails.
A letter has arrived.

en.usage: Birds, chickens, rabbits (historically counted as "winged animals")
en.notes: Rabbits are counted with 羽 because Buddhist monks declared them "birds" so they could eat them. 千羽鶴 (せんばづる) = 1000 folded paper cranes (a good-luck symbol). For 3, 6, 8, 10 there are alternative readings with ば/ぱ.
examples[].german: There are three ducks in the pond.
I folded a thousand cranes.

en.usage: TV episodes, anime episodes, stories, manga chapters
en.notes: Since わ begins with w, there are no sound changes. Often used with the prefix 第 (だい): 第一話, 第二話, etc.
examples[].german: I watched episode five of the anime.
This drama has twelve episodes in total.

en.notes: No sound changes. 割引 (わりびき) = discount is a very common word. 割り勘 (わりかん) = splitting the bill. In baseball, batting average is given in 割.
examples[].german: 80% of the students passed.
This product is 30% off.

en.notes: No sound changes. Cent is セント.
examples[].german: The coffee cost three euros.
The hotel costs 80 euros per night.

en.notes: No sound changes. 日本百名山 = the 100 famous mountains of Japan. For constellations: オリオン座, さそり座, etc.
examples[].german: This year I climbed three mountains.
You can see the constellation Orion.

en.meaning: pairs of chopsticks, bowls of food
en.usage: Pairs of chopsticks; formal meal sets
en.notes: Since ぜん already begins with a voiced consonant, there are no sound changes. Used both for pairs of chopsticks and for meal sets.
examples[].german: Three pairs of chopsticks, please.
Is one bowl of rice enough?
